 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Tonight, Estadio Banorte pulled out all the stops for the tribute Club América organized for one of its greatest icons: Guillermo Ochoa.
 The goalkeeper, who announced his retirement from soccer this year, received a standing ovation from the crowd before the match against Pachuca. He was visibly moved by a tifo featuring his image and the words "FOR13VER," a nod to his iconic number 13.
 As part of the celebrations, a mural of Paco Memo was unveiled at the Colossus of Santa Úrsula, where his name was also mounted on the stadium's facade.
 To conclude the tribute, Ochoa addressed the crowd at halftime, saying: "I want to thank the board, the people who work at the club, and everyone who made this moment possible. Thank you, because I will always carry this gesture in my heart. I want to thank my parents, who are up there, because I am here thanks to them. Thank you for enrolling me in América's soccer school. To my wife and children, who have been by my side every step of the way. To my family and friends who are here. And to the most important people: you, the fans."
 And so, the América youth academy graduate bid farewell to the club that gave him the opportunity to move to European soccer and also wear the national team's colors.
